title: Causality Guided Disentanglement for Cross-Platform Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: The paper measures cross-platform hate speech detection capabilities. It evaluates 'Religion' as one of eight primary target categories of hate speech, treating the specific target of hate (such as religious groups) as a platform-dependent variable that can be disentangled from the core invariant/causal features of hateful language to improve model generalization.
findings: The study found that the target distributions for hate speech (including religion) vary significantly across platforms. Current models tend to form spurious correlations and overly rely on specific identity words (e.g., 'jews'), which degrades their cross-platform generalization. By separating the platform-dependent target (such as religion) from the invariant properties of hate speech, their proposed model (CATCH) achieved better cross-platform detection compared to baseline models and large language models like GPT-4 and Falcon.
